newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche profits soar to six-year high.
newsitem.headline: Porsche profits soar to six-year high.

text.p: Porsche AG, making a clear statement about its return to financial health, said Friday that its profits soared to their highest level in six years on strong demand for its legendary 911 sports car.
The company said it made a staggering 2,190 percent gain in income to 48 million marks ($31.78 million) in the year ended July 31.

Although the profit was not great for a company its size, the earnings enabled Porsche to pay its first preferred dividend since 1992 and vindicated predictions of contined sharp profit growth this fiscal year.

Last year's earnings were the highest since 1989-1990, when it made 57 million marks ($37.7 million), and marked the biggest step yet in a comeback since the company lost 238.8 million marks ($158.1 million) in 1992-1993 and nearly went out of business.
Analysts said the profit figure, which was much greater than even Porsche had forecast, might have been larger, but the car maker has traditionally followed very conservative accounting procedures.

The company said the surge in profits was due entirely to Porsche's legendary 911 model -- a 30-year old design which the company has constantly updated. It produced a record 20,100 of them during the 1995-1996 business year.

Analysts attributed the strong 911 sales to an attractive range of configurations of the car, strong economic growth and demand for luxury cars, especially in the United States, Porsche's largest market.
